description: A broad, rectangular bench with sharp, rectilinear scarps on its western and southern edges. Measures approximately 200 m × 150 m. Visible in the hillshade as a low-relief plateau with paired convex (embankment) and concave (ditch) curvature signatures framing a flat surface.

A sinuous linear feature running north–south over ~650 m. In the DTM it appears as a consistent 4–6 m wide depression; in the NIR band it corresponds to a darker moisture-retentive line. Likely a canal or drainage ditch connecting small headwater swales.

A series of three parallel low ridges, each ~2–3 m high and spaced ~25 m apart, aligned NW–SE. Slightly elevated in the DTM and exhibiting corresponding vegetation stress lines in the NIR. May represent raised-field beds for upland agriculture.
